domain: A1 player health: photosensitivity (flashes, red flashes, warning, reduce-flashing, motion and shake options) in the committed tree, the live public site and the private LAN kit

risks.title: Live /play/ build reads at or over 3 flashes a second on the team's own analyser
risks.player_impact: A photosensitive player who clicks through the warning at /play/ can meet scenes the project's own check reads at 3 to 3.5 flashes a second; the signature clip in the shipped reduced mode reads 3/3/3, at the limit with no margin.
where: tools/site-pin.mjs:30 (at 72a4d1e4: owner path reads no recorded pass)
risks.evidence: curl: /play/ serves a 9.0 MB index.pck whose build_info is commit 257a766 with lock_reduce_flashing true, behind a click-through. Nightly runs on 257a766c recorded worst seconds of 3.5 (normal clips); the signature clip reads reduced 3/3/3; the last full recorded pass (d3f1ca0e, waivers expired 2026-10-22) has FAIL rows in reduced mode too.
risks.needs_outside_expert: A recognised photosensitivity analysis (the kind WCAG's Understanding page lists, e.g. Harding FPA or PEAT) of the live build's worst scenes at full screen; it would be S1 if the gate were missing or skippable.

risks.title: Main's Reduce flashing no longer slows the scenery sweep (regression since 2026-10-22)
risks.player_impact: In builds made from main (the private LAN builds for Orb and Orb 2, and any future public pin), the locked-on reduced mode lets scenery cross the screen as fast as full effects, the mitigation tied to the collapse fly-past reading of 4.5 flashes a second.
risks.evidence: HEAD sets SCROLL_MAX_REDUCED = 0.045, equal to SCROLL_MAX, with the comment that flash work is paused; the live pin had 0.03 with the comment citing 4.5 flashes a second on the collapse clip. The facade pan haze that would soften window-grid sweeps ships off. Introduced in 5fe08207 (2026-10-22).
risks.needs_outside_expert: A recognised analyser run of a fast city pursuit and collapse on a main-built locked export.

risks.title: The flash limiter cannot see several large-change sources, so it does not bound total flashes
risks.player_impact: Hard camera cuts, split-screen swaps, scenery sweeping past a moving camera, collapses, the calm-form beam body and the worn-aura flicker are not counted, so a second can exceed 3 flashes even when the register is within budget.
risks.evidence: The register's own header says it cannot see scenery sweeping past a moving camera unless the maker asks; camera asks only for cut_dip, cut_in_panel and transform_cut. In reduced mode beams and clashes skip the ask entirely, so their remaining body is uncounted. The aura flicker stops only for reduced_motion, not for Reduce flashing.
risks.needs_outside_expert: A recognised analyser on captured full-screen play; the in-game counter is a design aid, not proof.

risks.title: The off switch and the 2026-11-15 expiry cannot take the playable build down while CI is broken
risks.player_impact: If a worse flash is found, or when the owner-set expiry passes, running the documented kill switch and pushing will not remove /play/, because deploy needs every CI job and none run; only a manual Pages unpublish would.
risks.evidence: site-offline.mjs says to commit and push the file to publish it; the deploy job needs qa, sim, data, flash, godot-parity, net, world and site. The expiry is only a CI failure message, not an automatic takedown, and nothing scheduled redeploys Pages.

risks.title: LAN builds switch on the meteor trail's 'loud' profile, which never asks the flash register
risks.player_impact: Orb and Orb 2's LAN builds draw the meteor ribbon with wide bright spans kept at full strength on planet-scale launches, an effect the main game ships off and which is not budgeted against other flashes.
risks.evidence: The kit patches _word to 'loud' ahead of the web check, so page_word() returns 'loud' on the desktop build, which turns meteor_burn_enabled on; meteor.gd and meteor_view.gd contain no register ask. The profile is described as a set for Orb to judge in a private preview.

risks.title: In a drawn 2v2, each other fight gets its own flash register, so the screen budget is not shared
risks.player_impact: If other fights are drawn (dev flag now, planned per HEAD's 2v2 plan), two registers each grant their own budget on one screen, roughly doubling the allowed flashes.
risks.evidence: stage_feed creates VfxHub.new() per other fight and each hub constructs a fresh VfxFlashRegistry; _sync copies switches but not the register. Off by default (--others or a local page word).

risks.title: The public README says the hosted build is offline while /play/ is live
risks.player_impact: A parent or player reading the public repo is told there is no playable build, while one is reachable from the About page and by URL, which weakens the safety message.
risks.evidence: README.md:7 says the hosted build is offline for now; the live root says a limited test build is up, /about/ links ../play/, and /play/ serves the engine.

risks.title: Red-flash refusal is a colour heuristic applied only to sources that ask
risks.player_impact: A dark saturated red (red channel 0.55 or less) passes the test, and red-orange effects that never ask (fire, embers, scorch) are not checked at all; no red screen tint was found.
risks.evidence: is_red() requires r > 0.55 with g and b under 0.45 r on stored values, whereas WCAG's working definition is R/(R+G+B) >= 0.8 plus a u'v' change over 0.2. The project's own recorded clips all read red 0.
risks.needs_outside_expert: A recognised analyser's red-flash channel would settle it.

risks.title: Anyone building from the public source gets an unlocked build with full effects selectable
risks.player_impact: A self-built copy defaults to Reduce flashing on but lets the player turn it off (normal budget 2.5 weight, 3 big, 6 flashes a second) and honours the notice-skipping command-line words on desktop.
risks.evidence: The committed lock_reduce_flashing is false; only the site, desktop and LAN packaging steps flip it to true. bypass_allowed() returns true off the web when unlocked.

checked_ok.area: Runtime flash register exists and is conservative for the sources that ask
checked_ok.why: Area weight uses 21,824 px (25% of 341x256 at 1024x768, matching WCAG Note 1), sums across the whole screen, refuses red, and in reduced mode allows at most 1.0 weight, 1 big and 3 flashes per 60 ticks.

checked_ok.area: Register runs every tick in shipped builds, with no switch to disable it
checked_ok.why: begin_tick runs from the VFX hub, or from the host when VFX is off; no feature flag or preview switch was found that bypasses it.

checked_ok.area: Reduce flashing is locked on in every player build path
checked_ok.where: live index.pck (lock_reduce_flashing true); tools/site-pin.mjs:85-91 at 72a4d1e4; net/tools/lan_kit.mjs:106-111; .github/workflows/desktop-builds.yml:64-69
checked_ok.why: Site, LAN and desktop packaging flip the lock and refuse if it fails; the menu forces it true and the F8 legacy key is refused when locked (ui/hud/ui_hud.gd:1746-1748; render/core/main.gd:1587).

checked_ok.area: Web warning gate on the live /play/ page
checked_ok.why: An opaque dialog states the finding and says do not play if photosensitive; the engine starts only from 'I understand, start' on every load (no autoplay, no remembered skip), with 'Not now' leading away.

checked_ok.where: ui/hud/ui_hud.gd:431-436,1508-1548; ui/widgets/ui_menu.gd:8-9; live pck menu_notice text
checked_ok.why: The start menu carries the notice once per session before any play, with no timeout and no default focus; URL bypass words are ignored on a public host and on locked builds.

checked_ok.area: Beams and clashes in reduced mode
checked_ok.why: Under Reduce flashing they never get the bright white form, and the beam's two-tint ripple is 2 Hz or slower.
The prompt pulse is 1.4 Hz, the large legend holds 3 s and rests 2 s, the beat ring ramps instead of blinking, and the divider slam asks the register (refused in reduced mode).

checked_ok.area: No lightning, full-screen white or red screen tint
checked_ok.where: grep over render/, ui/, data/ (lightning, whiteout, screen_flash, strobe, vignette, low_hp)
checked_ok.why: Only comments forbidding lightning and white flashes were found; data/art/auras.json:9 and data/vfx/transform.json:3 rule out white or lightning flashes.

checked_ok.area: Catastrophe light events and slow effects
checked_ok.why: World-scale light is one event per 2 s with at least a 0.3 s rise and 1 s fall; clash bursts come at most 1.33 a second; the worn-aura dropout is at most 1.5 a second per fighter.

Shake defaults to 2 of 10 and has an on/off box on the first screen plus a 0-10 slider in Settings; Reduced motion (default off, in Settings only) quarters the shake and calms cuts, swings and the sky.

checked_ok.area: What else the public site serves
checked_ok.why: /, /bench/, /band/, /404.html and unknown paths share one holding page with no links and no game; /play/ is noindex. GitHub shows no releases, and the only Actions artifact is a web template.

limits: I did not run the game or any analyser; every flash count above comes from the project's own recorded readings of its own unrecognised tool (tools/flash/wcag.js says it is not Harding or PEAT).

WCAG 2.3.1 can't be certified from code: the register follows the general-flash area rule for the sources that ask, but whether the screen as a whole meets 2.3.1 needs a recognised analyser on full-screen captures (technique G15).

The 21,824 px threshold is a fraction of a 1024x768 reference frame; the Understanding page notes that viewers closer than the reference distance are affected by flashes that pass, which matters for TVs, a docked Steam Deck and large monitors. Not assessed.
Excluded folders (docs/legal, docs/accessibility, docs/qa, docs/ep, audit, homework) were not read, so the source table of what each refused flash still draws is unverified.
For the live pin 257a766c I checked the register constants, the notice and bypass code, the scroll cap and the menu rows; the rest of its camera and cut code was assumed to match HEAD.
I did not inspect the LAN builds themselves, only net/tools/lan_kit.mjs. I did not re-verify the ci.yml YAML breakage (that is the auditor's established fact), only that deploy needs every job.
